title: The lower truncation kernel of a perfect affine lift is finite locally free
statement: Let X = Spec(A) be affine [def-pc-scheme] and let P^\bullet be a bounded-above complex of finite free A-modules [def-pc-perfect-complex] whose restriction to a quasi-compact open U represents a perfect object E of D(\mathcal O_U) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex] of Tor amplitude in [a,b] [lem-pc-affine-tor-amplitude-criterion]. For any r<a, put K = Im(P^{r-1} \to P^r); on U the sheaf \widetilde K|_U coincides with the kernel of \widetilde{P^r}|_U \to \widetilde{P^{r+1}}|_U (the two A-modules Ker(P^r \to P^{r+1}) and Im(P^{r-1} \to P^r) need not agree on X). The restriction to U of the quasi-coherent sheaf \widetilde K associated to K is flat and of finite presentation, hence finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

proof.text: Write X=Spec(A). The given bounded-above finite-free complex P^\bullet represents E|_U, and [lem-pc-affine-tor-amplitude-criterion] transfers the stated Tor amplitude [a,b] between the sheaf and module formulations.

source.place: Tag 08ED proof, first paragraph and the invocation of Lemma 08E9

proof.text: Choose r<a and set K=Im(P^{r-1} \to P^r). Since the cohomology of the represented object vanishes below a, the complex is exact at degree r on U, so the associated sheaf \widetilde K|_U identifies with Ker(\widetilde{P^r}|_U \to \widetilde{P^{r+1}}|_U); this equality is only asserted after restriction to U, not as an equality of A-modules on all of X.

source.place: Tag 08ED proof, definition of K and exactness below the Tor-amplitude range

proof.text: Let f\in A with D(f)\subseteq U; such principal opens cover U. By [lem-sc-affine-truncation-kernel-flat] (the last-one-flat lemma), applied to the same complex and the same r<a, the A_f-module K_f is flat and finitely presented, hence a finite projective A_f-module by [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-flat-module-projective] (Stacks Tag 00NX). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] there are g_1,\dots,g_s\in A_f generating the unit ideal with each (K_f)_{g_i} finite free, so \widetilde K|_{D(f)} is free of finite rank on each D(g_i)\subseteq D(f). Hence \widetilde K|_U is locally free of finite rank, i.e. finite locally free; in particular it is flat and of finite presentation, its local sections being localizations of the flat finitely presented modules K_f.
